children: President Donald Trump has named Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to lead a new White House artificial intelligence task force, giving the intelligence chief a prominent role in shaping the administration’s approach to AI risks and U.S. competitiveness.

Clayton, who became intelligence director in August, will oversee a panel expected to deliver recommendations within 120 days, according to The Wall Street Journal. The group, which the administration calls the “Super Intelligence Force,” will examine both the opportunities and potential dangers posed by increasingly powerful AI systems.

The initiative comes amid growing concern in Washington about AI safety. Researchers and lawmakers from both parties have raised alarms about the potential for advanced systems to cause serious harm, while the administration has generally resisted regulations that could slow U.S. development of the technology.

Trump has emphasized competition with China as a central consideration in AI policy. He has argued that burdensome regulation could undermine the U.S. technology industry and recently rejected the idea of working with Chinese President Xi Jinping on joint AI governance.

The task force could offer an early indication of whether Washington will tighten oversight of AI developers or continue favoring a relatively light regulatory approach. Its recommendations could affect companies developing advanced models, cloud and data-center operators, semiconductor suppliers and cybersecurity firms. The 120-day review also creates a potential policy catalyst for technology stocks if it produces significant proposals on safety, security or reporting requirements.

Clayton's panel will examine existing systems for reporting AI-related security breaches, cyberattacks and other incidents. It also will recommend ways the federal government can improve its response using existing legal authority, suggesting at least some measures may not require new legislation.

The group will include senior administration officials, with Emil Michael, Scott Kupor and Federal Trade Commission Chair Andrew Ferguson serving as vice chairs. Vice President JD Vance, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles are also expected to participate. Outside advisers will include former AI adviser David Sacks and former Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice.
